topology_reasoning.what_is_it: A symmetric multi-rail (supermode) coupler / waveguide-array coupler. Reading the transverse cross-section (a vertical cut at mid-length, image x=2400) top->bottom there are, symmetric about the mid-line y=2.0um: [array A: 5 thin waveguides] | [slab/rail B: one wide guide] | [array C: 5 thin waveguides, centered] | [slab/rail D] | [array E: 5 thin waveguides]. So 3 identical 5-wire arrays separated by 2 wide rails.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: The CENTER array C (5 wires) runs straight the full 120um (verified present from image x=319 to x=4460). The two OUTER bundles (rail B + array A above; rail D + array E below) run straight and parallel to C over a central coupling region, then at BOTH ends adiabatically bend AWAY (S-bend) toward the top/bottom chip edge and exit off-frame. Light launched in an outer bundle couples into the central array over the parallel-run (transfer/coupling) length; the flared ends are the access routing. It is mirror-symmetric top<->bottom about y=2.0um.

measured_features_um.flare_length_each_end_um: ~6-8 (bundle bends to the y=0/y=4 edge and exits)

function_knobs: gap (edge-to-edge spacing between rails/arrays; the coupling gap)
delta_length (arm path-length imbalance between the two outer coupled bundles; 0 in the figure => balanced; this is the Phase-B FSR/phase knob)
